overview: The MPU6050 (often sold on a small blue 'GY-521' breakout) combines a 3-axis accelerometer and a 3-axis gyroscope in one chip — six degrees of freedom total, hence '6-DOF.' The accelerometer measures gravity/acceleration but is noisy and drifts under motion; the gyroscope measures rotation rate cleanly in the short term but drifts over time. Neither one alone gives a reliable orientation reading, which is why almost every project using this sensor runs a sensor fusion algorithm (like a Kalman or complementary filter) in software to combine both into a stable tilt/orientation estimate — a genuinely important concept this chip is most people's first introduction to.
simpleSummary: A chip that senses both tilt and rotation, commonly used to measure a robot's orientation.

specifications.operatingVoltage: 3.3V (breakout boards commonly add a regulator for 5V tolerance)
specifications.magnetometer: None (see MPU9250 for a 9-DOF version with a built-in compass)

pinMap.name: XDA
pinMap.function: Auxiliary I2C data line, for connecting a secondary sensor (e.g. an external magnetometer) that the MPU6050 can read on the host's behalf.
pinMap.gotcha: Rarely used in beginner projects — safe to leave unconnected.

pinMap.name: AD0
pinMap.function: I2C address select — LOW (default/grounded) sets address 0x68, HIGH sets 0x69.
pinMap.gotcha: Tie HIGH to run two MPU6050s on the same I2C bus without an address conflict.

pinMap.name: INT
pinMap.function: Interrupt output, configurable to fire on new-data-ready or motion-detection events.

useCases.title: Self-balancing robot
useCases.scenario: Fuse accelerometer and gyroscope readings to estimate tilt angle for a balancing control loop.

useCases.title: Drone/flight controller stabilization
useCases.scenario: Core sensor for basic DIY flight controllers before upgrading to a 9-DOF or fusion-chip sensor.

useCases.title: Step counter / activity tracker
useCases.scenario: Detect motion patterns from raw acceleration data.

oftenConfusedWith: MPU9250 (adds a magnetometer for absolute heading)
oftenUpgradedTo: BNO055 (does sensor fusion onboard, no software filter needed)
